answers.text: Give me exactly three lines every time, same order — delivery date, item and quantity, then any change from the original order. Same date format every time, item named just like on the order, and if the email doesn't mention one of the three, write 'not stated' instead of guessing or leaving it blank. That way it's tidy and quick to read.

The memo should always have the same four lines in the same order — date, amount, category, submitter — with a total added at the end. The total is just the sum of the amounts for that week, same currency, shown to two decimals. Even if two people write it up separately, the layout and the total should come out the same.

Something here doesn't add up, so I wouldn't send it as is. It's not the price — 100 times 48.50 does come to 4,850, that part's fine — it's the dates that are the problem, the 19th and 'three days out from today' don't quite sit together with a call on the 14th.
The 62 versus 54 checks out fine, about a 15% jump. But 3 late out of 62 doesn't come to 97% — it's closer to 95%, so that number's wrong.
I'd sign off Output 2 — the one with 612,000 and 25,100 in it, not just the 4.1%. Output 1 only gives the percentage, no sales figure or returns figure to check it against.
I'd send Reply 2 without checking further — it's got the order number and the credit reference in it. Reply 1 says 'this was entirely our error' but there's nothing in it to check that claim against.
1. Delivery address — no. 2. Sales total, aggregate — yes, fine. 3. Next quarter's pricing — no, not out yet. 4. Spec sheet — yes, already public. 5. Colleague's mobile — no.

I'd be careful putting anything from the contract into a tool we haven't checked yet — pricing especially, I wouldn't paste that in without asking first. Best to check with IT if the tool's even allowed for this kind of thing before doing anything else.
I'd have the weekly totals cross-checked against the depot system directly, not just read over. That check happens before the report goes to the manager on Friday, not after it's sent.

Step 1 worries me most — if the AI misreads the order email, the wrong numbers carry through everything after it. Step 4, the automatic send, is really where it needs a proper look before anything goes out.
